How to attempt a Relations and Functions case study

Case Study: The Team Contact List

Read the passage carefully, then answer the 5 MCQs in the test below.

Four members of a project team — labelled 1,2,3 and 4 — use an internal messaging app. The app stores a relation R on the set A={1,2,3,4}, where (x,y)∈ R means “member x has saved member y's number”. After the first week the stored relation is R={(1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(4,4),(1,2),(2,1),(2,3),(3,2)}. The administrator wants to describe this relation using the three standard properties studied in class — reflexive, symmetric and transitive — and to decide whether it is an equivalence relation. If it is not, she would like to know the fewest new entries that would turn it into one, and how the team would then split into groups where everyone has saved everyone else in the group. She checks each property against the actual pairs rather than guessing from the picture.

questions.q: Judging only from the stored pairs, the relation R is
questions.explanation: Diagonal pairs (1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(4,4) are all present, so R is reflexive. Every off-diagonal pair has its reverse: (1,2)&(2,1) and (2,3)&(3,2), so R is symmetric. It is not transitive (see (iii)), so R is reflexive and symmetric only. (a).

options: it is a subset of A× A
for every (x,y)∈ R the reverse (y,x) is also in R
questions.explanation: Symmetry is precisely the statement that whenever (x,y)∈ R, the reverse pair (y,x) also lies in R; both mixed pairs here satisfy it. (c).

questions.q: R fails to be transitive because
questions.explanation: (1,2)∈ R and (2,3)∈ R, so transitivity would require (1,3)∈ R; but (1,3)∉ R, so transitivity fails. (b).

questions.q: The least number of ordered pairs that must be added to make R an equivalence relation is
questions.explanation: To repair transitivity within {1,2,3} we must add (1,3) and (3,1); these two pairs also keep symmetry, and then {1,2,3} is fully related. Hence 2 pairs suffice. (c).

questions.q: After that completion, the equivalence classes of the team are
questions.explanation: Members 1,2,3 become mutually related while 4 stays alone, so the classes are {1,2,3} and {4}. (d).
